Actual vapour pressure

Source: R/forcing-derived.R
ef_ea.Rd

Computes the actual vapour pressure of the air \(e_a\) from the humidity data available, with the FAO-56 equations:

  • ef_ea_dewpoint(): from the dew point temperature (any time step);

  • ef_ea_rh(): from the air temperature and relative humidity of the same period (hourly or shorter);

  • ef_ea_daily(): from the daily extreme temperatures and relative humidities, with an explicit method ("rhmax_rhmin", "rhmax", "rhmin", "rhmean" or "rhmean_tmean");

  • ef_ea_tmin(): from the minimum temperature, only when humidity data are missing, with an explicit aridity correction k0.

Usage

ef_ea_dewpoint(dewpoint_temperature)

ef_ea_rh(air_temperature, relative_humidity)

ef_ea_tmin(tmin, k0)

ef_ea_daily(tmin, tmax = NULL, rh_max, rh_min = NULL, method)

Arguments

dewpoint_temperature

Numeric. Dew point temperature [degrees Celsius], finite and > -237.3.

air_temperature

Numeric. Air temperature of the period [degrees Celsius], finite and > -237.3.

relative_humidity

Numeric. Relative humidity of the same period [%], finite and >= 0. Values above 100 % are computed (they are a quality-control matter, EF_WS_RH_GT100), never truncated.

tmin, tmax

Numeric. Daily minimum and maximum air temperatures [degrees Celsius], finite and > -237.3; tmin <= tmax. tmax is not used by method = "rhmax" and tmin not by method = "rhmin"; they may then be omitted (NULL).

k0

Numeric. Aridity correction \(K_0\) [degC] subtracted from tmin to approximate the dew point, finite and >= 0. FAO-56 (annex 6, Eq. 6-6) gives 0 degC for humid and sub-humid climates and 2 degC for arid and semi-arid climates (chapter 3: 2-3 degC). No default: the choice depends on the climate of the site.

rh_max, rh_min

Numeric. Daily maximum and minimum relative humidity [%], finite and >= 0. rh_min is not used by method = "rhmax" and rh_max not by method = "rhmin"; they may then be omitted (NULL).

method

Character, no default. Formulation of ef_ea_daily():

  • "rhmax_rhmin": FAO-56 Eq. 17, from tmin, tmax, rh_max and rh_min (recommended by FAO-56);

  • "rhmax": FAO-56 Eq. 18, from tmin and rh_max only (when rh_min is doubtful);

  • "rhmin": ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eq. 13, from tmax and rh_min only (when only good daily minimum humidities are available; less desirable than Eqs. 11-12 of the report);

  • "rhmean": FAO-56 Eq. 19, from the mean relative humidity (rh_max + rh_min) / 2 and the mean saturation vapour pressure (the least desirable of the FAO-56 forms; not recommended in the ASCE-EWRI standardized procedure);

  • "rhmean_tmean": ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eq. 14, from the mean relative humidity (rh_max + rh_min) / 2 and the saturation vapour pressure at the mean temperature (tmax + tmin) / 2 (the form of the standardized procedure when only the mean humidity is usable).

Value

A numeric vector of actual vapour pressure \(e_a\) [kPa] with the common length of the inputs, keeping their dim.

Details

With \(e^\circ(T)\) the saturation vapour pressure of ef_es() (FAO-56 Eq. 11): $$e_a = e^\circ(T_{dew})$$ (Eq. 14; ef_ea_dewpoint()), $$e_a = e^\circ(T_{hr}) \frac{RH_{hr}}{100}$$ (Eq. 54; annex 5, Eq. 5-3: temperature and humidity of the same period, preferably one hour or less; ef_ea_rh()), $$e_a = \frac{e^\circ(T_{min}) \frac{RH_{max}}{100} + e^\circ(T_{max}) \frac{RH_{min}}{100}}{2}$$ (Eq. 17; "rhmax_rhmin"), $$e_a = e^\circ(T_{min}) \frac{RH_{max}}{100}$$ (Eq. 18; "rhmax"), $$e_a = e^\circ(T_{max}) \frac{RH_{min}}{100}$$ (ASCE-EWRI 2005, Eq. 13; "rhmin"), $$e_a = \frac{RH_{mean}}{100} \frac{e^\circ(T_{max}) + e^\circ(T_{min})}{2}, \quad RH_{mean} = \frac{RH_{max} + RH_{min}}{2}$$ (Eq. 19; "rhmean"), $$e_a = \frac{RH_{mean}}{100} e^\circ\left(\frac{T_{max} + T_{min}}{2}\right)$$ (ASCE-EWRI 2005, Eqs. 14 and 2; "rhmean_tmean"), and $$e_a = e^\circ(T_{min} - K_0)$$ (Eq. 48; annex 6, Eq. 6-6; ef_ea_tmin()). The last one assumes that the dew point is close to the minimum temperature, which holds only at well-watered reference sites; FAO-56 recommends it only when humidity data are missing.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The report gives the same forms for the standardized equation: Eq. 8 and Eq. 38 (dew point; FAO-56 Eq. 14), Eq. 41 (hourly relative humidity; FAO-56 Eq. 54), Eq. 11 (FAO-56 Eq. 17) and Eq. 12 (FAO-56 Eq. 18), with the preference rankings of its Tables 3 (daily) and 4 (hourly) (pp. 12, 30). It adds Eq. 13 ("rhmin") and replaces the mean-humidity form: Eq. 14 ("rhmean_tmean") uses \(e^\circ(T_{mean})\), and the FAO-56 Eq. 19 form ("rhmean") is "not recommended in the standardized procedure" (p. 17). The estimate from the minimum temperature is described in its Appendix E (not read; ef_ea_tmin() stays a FAO-56 form). The psychrometric forms (report Eqs. 9-10, 39-40) are not implemented.

FAO-56 and dev/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md section 5 recommend regionalising the actual vapour pressure (nearly constant during the day), not the relative humidity, which depends on the temperature.

Missing values propagate. Non-numeric, empty or incompatible inputs raise earthflux_input_error; temperatures <= -237.3, negative humidities, negative k0, tmin > tmax or infinite values raise earthflux_domain_error. A missing or unknown method raises earthflux_missing_input or earthflux_unknown_method; an input required by the method and not supplied raises earthflux_missing_input.

Verification status

VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eqs. 14, 17, 18, 19, 48 and 54; annex 6, Eq. 6-6; dev/specs/weather-forcing.md 4.4, cases V3 and V17). ef_ea_tmin() is verified as an equation; its use is restricted to missing humidity data and k0 is always explicit. "rhmin" and "rhmean_tmean": VERIFICADA (ASCE-EWRI, 2005, Eqs. 13 and 14, pp. 16-17); the forms shared with FAO-56 are also ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eqs. 8, 11, 12, 38 and 41 (pp. 13, 15, 30, 32).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Other derived meteorological variables: ef_dewpoint(), ef_es(), ef_es_slope(), ef_psychrometric(), ef_ra_daily(), ef_ra_period(), ef_rso(), ef_wind_2m()

Examples

# FAO-56 example 5: Tmin = 18, Tmax = 25 degrees C, RHmax = 82,
# RHmin = 54 %
ef_ea_daily(tmin = 18, tmax = 25, rh_max = 82, rh_min = 54,
            method = "rhmax_rhmin")
#> [1] 1.701536
ef_ea_daily(tmin = 18, tmax = 25, rh_max = 82, rh_min = 54,
            method = "rhmean")
#> [1] 1.778801
ef_ea_daily(tmin = 18, rh_max = 82, method = "rhmax")
#> [1] 1.692471
# ASCE-EWRI (2005) forms: Eq. 13 and Eq. 14
ef_ea_daily(tmax = 25, rh_min = 54, method = "rhmin")
#> [1] 1.7106
ef_ea_daily(tmin = 18, tmax = 25, rh_max = 82, rh_min = 54,
            method = "rhmean_tmean")
#> [1] 1.743805

# From the dew point, and from hourly temperature and humidity
ef_ea_dewpoint(15)
#> [1] 1.705346
ef_ea_rh(air_temperature = 38, relative_humidity = 52)
#> [1] 3.444874

# Minimum temperature, arid site (k0 = 2 degrees C)
ef_ea_tmin(tmin = 12, k0 = 2)
#> [1] 1.227963
